text: It is in the same manner that the razor of insight wisdom has to be whetted on the sharpening stone of the Satipatthana — four ways of paying attention — sutta.
Dhono na hi tena mannati yadidam ditthasutam mutesu va — the arahant does not imagine 'thereby', namely, by whatever is seen, heard and sensed.

In the seen there will be just the seen... Then you will not be by it. And when you are not by it, you are not in it. And when you are not in it, you are neither here nor there nor in between. This itself is the end of suffering.
With the idea of sharpening the razor, if one grabs it tightly and rubs it on the sharpening stone, it will only become blunt. Paramasana, holding on, grabbing, is something like that.

What tranquillity meditation does, is to temporarily calm them down and derive some sort of happiness. That too is necessary from the point of view of concentration, to do away with restlessness and the like, but it does not dispel not seeing how it works. That is why, in insight meditation, one tries to understand things the mind makes for what they are by dispelling not seeing how it works. The more one sees things the mind makes as things the mind makes, not seeing how it works is dispelled, and the more one dispels not seeing how it works, the things the mind makes lose their significance as things the mind makes.

The third combined movement ensures that those parts of the blade still untouched by the stone will also get duly sharpened.
